title: Slanted Pull? Dot Product Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Pull a suitcase by its handle, tow a toy car on a string, push a lawn mower by its long handle. You pull at a slant, but the thing moves along the ground. So how much of Aarav's 40 N pull really moves his suitcase forward? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we answer it with one small tool: the scalar or dot product.

A torch and a stick show what a shadow (projection) is. Then a live suitcase simulation raises the handle from 0 to 60 to 90 degrees while the readout and an F cos theta graph move together, with a slow-mo replay. We derive A.B = AB cos theta step by step, see why it is a number and not an arrow, compare 60 and 120 degrees side by side, prove i.i = 1 and i.j = 0, and reach A.B = AxBx + AyBy + AzBz. Then a worked example (angle between two vectors), the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question on the component of one vector along another, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET.
